history.period: Inaugurated 31 May 1997 (founded under Sri Madhu Pandit Dasa; opened by President Shankar Dayal Sharma)
history.summary: One of the largest ISKCON temples in the world, located on Hare Krishna Hill, Chord Road, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru. Established under Sri Madhu Pandit Dasa and inaugurated on 31 May 1997 by then President of India Shankar Dayal Sharma. The modern granite-and-glass complex has five shrines - Sri Radha Krishnachandra, Krishna Balarama, Nitai Gauranga, Srinivasa Govinda and Prahlada Narasimha - a 17-metre gold-plated dhwaja-stambha (flagstaff), gold-plated kalashas, a lecture hall for Bhagavad Gita discourses, an amphitheatre, a Vedic museum, and free Krishna prasadam for visitors. ISKCON Bangalore is closely associated with the Akshaya Patra Foundation, which provides midday meals to schoolchildren across India. CSV town 'Bengaluru' is correct. Coordinates (13.009787, 77.551117) are from the temple's official listing. Note: ISKCON Bangalore is a distinct legal entity from ISKCON Mumbai - some sources describe organisational disputes (verify before asserting details).

name: ISKCON Bangalore (Sri Radha Krishna Chandra Temple)
town_description: Bengaluru (Bangalore), the capital of Karnataka, is India's major technology hub, nicknamed the Silicon Valley of India, and also known as the Garden City for its parks and tree-lined avenues. Founded as a fortified town by Kempe Gowda in 1537, it blends heritage landmarks - the Bangalore Palace, Vidhana Soudha, and the 16th-century Bull Temple - with a modern metropolis. It has one of India's busiest airports and is a major domestic and international tourist gateway.
